messages:
Maya R: Heads-up: after yesterday's runtime tweak I see a perf regression on mixtral-8b when head_dim is 70 (non-8/16-aligned). p99 increased ~35%.
Jordan C: CI flame: https://ci.internal/redwood/profiles/2329987654/flame.svg 1: flame shows a concentration in sdpa_masked_kernel during attention hotpath.
Liam P: Repro locally with a micro-bench harness. Command I used:
```
MODEL=mixtral-8b
SEQ=1024
HEAD_DIM=70
./bench --model $MODEL --seq $SEQ --head-dim $HEAD_DIM --warmup 3 --iters 30
```
Outcome: runtime prefers SDPA fallback because kernel_selector rejects flash_attn (head_dim fails requirement). sdpa p99 ~41ms vs flash ~21ms.
Carmen S: What exact selector rule fired? logs?
Maya R: Runtime log snippet:
```
kernel_selector: evaluating candidate=flash_attn
requirement: head_dim % 16 == 0 -> false
-> choose sdpa_masked_kernel (fallback)
```
We currently require %16 alignment for flash. Newer flash kernels can run with %8 alignment or with small padding; our conservative rule is forcing expensive fallbacks.
Jordan C: Agreed. Also note padding-to-16 inflates KV cache per-token size (stride increases), which worsens memory bandwidth for long contexts.
Liam P: I experimented with a local headpad policy that allows pad_to=8 for flash when (head_dim%8==0 after pad) and seq_len <= 512 or model in {mixtral,mistral,llama}. Numbers: p50 9.8ms->8.9ms, p99 42ms->23ms.
Maya R: Proposed quick mitigation:
- relax headpad policy: allow pad-to-8 for flash kernels in safe model/seq cases
- add per-model kernel preference override in model_profile so mixtral-8b can prefer flash_attn while we validate
- emit telemetry for fallback_reason to quantify how often sdpa/triton chosen and why
Jordan C: Patch sketch:
```
if candidate == flash_attn:
  pad_target = 8 if (model in small_align_ok) else 16
  allow_pad(pad_target) when seq_len <= 512 or model in small_align_ok
```
We need a feature-flagged rollout though.
Carmen S: Risks: RoPE correctness when we change alignment; we've seen subtle rotary scaling bugs depending on how heads align/pad. Also KV offsets and prefetch heuristics may need tuning when stride changes.
Liam P: I added a tiny prefetch heuristic tweak in my branch: recompute prefetch_window when per-head stride increases due to padding. Pseudocode:
```
if padded_stride > orig_stride:
  prefetch_window = max(16, floor(ideal_tokens / (padded_stride / orig_stride)))
```
This prevents compute starvation when KV memory layout gets wider.
Maya R: Testing plan:
- unit tests for kernel_selector cases with head_dim in {65,70,74,80}
- run RoPE/regression eval suite across seq lenses (512,1024,2048+)
- staging canary (10% traffic) for mixtral-8b with model_profile override -> prefer flash_attn
- monitor telemetry.fallback_reason, p50/p90/p99, and memory growth
Jordan C: I'll produce flamegraph diffs and hook up the perf-bench A/B harness for canary validation.
Liam P: I'll land the kvcache prefetch tweak and add allocator unit tests. Also include an opt-in config flag: runtime.experimental.pad_to_8_for_flash=true so we can flip quickly.
Carmen S: If any RoPE or correctness regressions show up in evals, revert the pad policy immediately. Alternative fallback: use Triton kernels that accept odd head dims without padding (slower than flash but avoid SDPA fallback).
Maya R: I'll open a PR with the headpad policy change + model_profile override + telemetry. Assigning reviewers @JordanC @LiamP. PR will include before/after perf numbers and canary plan.
perf-bot: perf/compare mixtral-8b headdim=70 seq=1024 p99_before=41.8ms p99_after=23.1ms delta=-44.8% :rocket:
Telemetry metric added: runtime.fallback_reason (counts by model & reason).
